subject: Re: Request: Clarification on LLM training, prompt logs & opt-out
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@fintechx.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-21T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Clarification: Do you train on customer prompts/responses?

Hi Sergio,

Hope you’re well. Our privacy/legal team has a few follow-ups for vendor onboarding (DPA review). Could you confirm the following at a high level so we can close the review: 

1) Do Redwood models or internal training pipelines ever incorporate customer prompts or model responses as training data for future models? If yes, under what conditions (opt-in/opt-out, aggregated/anonymized, retention windows)?
2) If we want to opt specific customer data out of any training/experiments, what is the process and SLA to effect that across Hosted and Dedicated modes?
3) Where (how long) are raw prompts and generated responses stored? Is there a default retention policy and is it configurable per account?
4) Do you provide any export/audit of prompts/responses for customer DPIA or SAR purposes?

We appreciate short, actionable answers and any pointer to evidence (SOC 2 artifact, data flow diagram, or policy). If helpful, cc’ing Legal: legal@fintechx.com.

Thanks —
Olivia
Senior Privacy Counsel, FintechX
From: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@fintechx.com>
Cc: FintechX Legal <legal@fintechx.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-21T11:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: Do you train on customer prompts/responses?

Olivia —

Thanks for the clear list. High-level responses below; I’ve looped in Monica from Customer Success and will route the security engineering artifacts via Neha. We can follow up with a short call if you prefer.

1) Training on customer prompts/responses:
- Hosted API: By default, customer prompts and responses are not used to train new base models. We may use aggregated telemetry for service quality (e.g., failure rates) but not raw prompt/response content.
- Dedicated/Private: Customer-managed Dedicated clusters and Private deployments do not feed back into our shared training pipelines.

2) Opt-out process / SLA:
- We support customer-level opt-out for Hosted customers via a formal request. Opt-out is applied at the tenant level and prevents any non-essential telemetry or aggregated sample usage for model training.
- SLA: opt-out requests are acknowledged within 48 hours and completed within 15 business days for Hosted accounts. For Dedicated/Private, opt-out is immediate by configuration (no data egress to our training stores).

3) Storage & retention of prompts/responses: 
- Default retention for raw prompts/responses in Hosted is 30 days (configurable to shorter windows on paid plans). We store structured logs (metadata, token counts) longer for billing/analytics per the DPA.
- For Dedicated: logs are owner-controlled; default deployments keep 7 days unless a customer sets otherwise.

4) Export/audit:
- We provide exports for DPIA/SAR purposes (subject to verification) via secure file transfer. We also supply retention and processing logs (timestamps, route, model version).

Attachments: I’m attaching a short SOC 2 policy excerpt and a diagram of the LLM data flows. Neha will add a more detailed evidence package if you need it for compliance review.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-soc2-training-policy-excerpt.pdf, dpa-llm-data-flow-diagram.png

Subject: Re: Clarification: Do you train on customer prompts/responses?

Sergio / Monica —

Adding a few security-precise clarifications to ensure Olivia/Legal have evidence-level statements: 
- We do not use identifiable customer prompt/response pairs to train production base models. Any experiments that use customer-provided content are done on anonymized copies and require explicit customer consent and an internal risk review.
- Retention policies: Hosted default 30 days; configurable via admin console (we can set 0 days on request). We record retention-change audit events in the customer audit log (kept per SOC 2 controls).
- Opt-out: For Hosted customers, filing a support ticket with the dataset preference flag triggers a pipeline that blocks content from joining any research/annotation queues. I confirm 15 business days operational window under current runbook.
- Evidence: I’m attaching the SOC 2 excerpt that maps to control CC6 (data lifecycle) and a short runbook extract describing the opt-out workflow. 

If FintechX needs signed confirmation for the DPA appendix, we can produce a one-page attestation (security-approved).

-Neha
Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that helps. A couple quick follow-ups from Legal: 

A) When you say 'aggregated telemetry' — can you confirm whether any identifiers (userIDs, accountIDs) are stripped before aggregation? If account-level signals are ever used to tune models (even non-content signals), we need visibility.
B) For the export path for SAR/DPIA: can you provide an estimated SLA and the format delivered? (e.g., JSONL of prompts with timestamps + manifest)

Also, can you provide the single-page attestation you mentioned? If possible, add a line indicating the effective date of the opt-out SLA (i.e., which policy version governs the 15 business day window).

Would prefer answers in writing before we book a legal ops call.

—Olivia
From: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@fintechx.com>
Cc: FintechX Legal <legal@fintechx.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-23T15:48:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: Do you train on customer prompts/responses?

Olivia / Legal —

Answers inline: 
A) Aggregated telemetry:
- Identifiers: accountIDs and userIDs are pseudonymized (hashed) before being included in aggregation sets. Raw identifiers are never part of model tuning datasets. We retain mapping keys in a restricted-access store for incident investigation (access logged).
- We do not use per-account signals to personalize base model weights. Signal telemetry can influence routing/feature flags at runtime (not model weights).

B) Export/SAR SLA & format:
- SLA: we acknowledge export requests within 2 business days and deliver exports within 10 business days for standard requests (subject to verification). Complex exports (large volumes or legal holds) are scoped separately.
- Format: standard export is JSONL with fields: timestamp, model_version, route, prompt_text (redacted if required), response_text (redacted if required), and a manifest CSV with token counts and retention policy applied. Files are delivered via an encrypted SFTP/secure link.

Attestation: Attached is a one-page attestation confirming: (1) no identifiable prompt/response pairs are used for production model training without consent; (2) opt-out SLA (15 business days) effective as of 2026-08-01; and (3) retention defaults. Let me know if Legal needs this on letterhead.

If helpful, we can run a short walkthrough of the export format and an example export (sanitized) next week.

Thanks,
Sergio
